name: Prototype

claims.claim_text: The usual output of a prototype is a decision to abandon the idea: most ideas are unworkable, and building a prototype rather than entering product development directly is what makes that discovery cheap.
claims.quote_verbatim: The role of most prototypes is to show that an idea is unworkable because most ideas are, are unworkable.
claims.speaker: Zack Freedman

claims.claim_text: A demonstration prototype does not need working features, but everything shown must be internally consistent and plausible, because a viewer who asks why an element is present has stopped evaluating the idea.
claims.quote_verbatim: none of it has to work. It just has to look sensible.
claims.speaker: Zack Freedman

claims.claim_text: Prototypes progress through distinguishable stages — proof of concept, looks-like, works-like — and communicating which stage a given unit represents is a substantive part of presenting it.
claims.quote_verbatim: the differences are between proof of concept, you know, looks like, works like

claims.claim_text: A looks-like, works-like prototype assembled from development modules is a legitimate deliverable in its own right when the quantity needed is around twenty and size is not constrained.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was Lego blocks put together for a fairly looks like works like prototype
claims.speaker: Elecia White

claims.claim_text: The term flight hardware is used to mean the final prototype, the version considered ready to go.
claims.quote_verbatim: the flight hardware is the kind of the final prototype
claims.speaker: Kent Lundberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Kent Lundberg - Luculent Linear Legacy

claims.claim_text: Holding the physical board is what exposes errors that months of looking at the schematic will not: the first assembled prototype of a design that had been reviewed on and off for months revealed roughly ten errors immediately.
claims.quote_verbatim: you immediately find like 10 errors
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Intel, EPA & Brown Field - Google's Ground Gurgitation

claims.claim_text: No amount of modelling substitutes for building the thing: a 3D model and a review are not equivalent to having a board in hand and working with it.
claims.quote_verbatim: nothing beats actually building the damn thing up and having a board and having a go at it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The same effect appears at the layout stage: problems are invisible until the work is under way and the physical object is in hand, at which point the design decision that looked fine reads as obviously wrong.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's the same thing with a prototype in your hand
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: Where board respins are cheap, spinning the board a couple of times deliberately beats insisting on correctness first time, because the two-month delay of getting it perfect is followed by a respin anyway.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's cheaper to just spin the board a couple times because we know it's going to happen anyways.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: On a cheap prototype the correct discipline is to release the design before it is finished, accept that some of it will be broken, and repair it with bodge wires; where only one or two expensive turns are available the calculation changes and more verification time is warranted.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're doing a cheap proto, yeah, just pull the trigger, man
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A partially finished circuit is still worth fabricating, because a board that can be populated in part, fitted into a case and handled answers questions that the unfinished design cannot.
claims.quote_verbatim: the circuit will be half finished. We'll order the board because we want a board.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Practice on prototype rigour varies widely between engineers, from deliberately rough first articles to a standard that accepts nothing less than a final-quality board and bill of materials even for a one-off.
claims.quote_verbatim: nothing less than an absolutely perfect final PCB and BOM is good enough for a prototype
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Hand-built first prototypes are expected to be crude enough to be embarrassing, and that is not evidence of poor work.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've got a few prototypes to make the first one that were hand built in almost embarrassingly
claims.speaker: Jonathan Georgino

claims.claim_text: Deliberate simplification is a valid prototype technique: brute-forcing every ground together produces a functional board with a higher noise floor rather than blocking progress on a grounding scheme that would take a full review to get right.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm just going to brute force all the grounds together. And that'll be good enough for my first prototype.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Radiation Chips & Old Package Types - Technocratic Toilet Troubleshooting

claims.claim_text: At the prototype stage, a reflexively chosen part carries little consequence and can be revisited later; the exception is a processor, where memory ceilings and switching costs make the choice expensive to reverse.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think that's almost always okay for prototypes
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The danger is not the reflexive prototype choice itself but carrying it into production without ever re-examining it.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's when you say, I'm not going to take a look at this again. That's when you can really get into trouble.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Simulation earns its cost where placing the circuit on a board is expensive or where a respin is not available, so a day of simulation buys a higher probability that the first prototype works.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't afford to re-spin it you've got to get it right the first time
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: EE Movies, Part Rants and SPICE.

claims.claim_text: Simulating a converter and going straight to production without a prototype is a step taken under schedule pressure rather than a recommended path.
claims.quote_verbatim: I simulated a power converter circuit in LT Spice and I didn't have time to prototype it. And I just put it into production.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Reducing cycle time is what makes prototyping effective: where a part in a leadless package cannot be breadboarded, the sooner it is on a board the sooner it is known whether the design is broken and the sooner that feeds back into a fix.
claims.quote_verbatim: the faster you get it on your board, the faster you know if it's broken or not
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Prior Art, Wafer Fabs and Guns - Whimsical Wafer Waffling

claims.claim_text: Some designs cannot be prototyped on a breadboard at all, which sets a floor on the time and money any attempt requires.
claims.quote_verbatim: you won't prototype this on a breadboard right don't even think about it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Headless Units and Baseless Batteries - KiCad Kickoff Kopophobia

claims.claim_text: Thorough verification means building every circuit rather than trusting the design: a book's worth of projects was validated by physically constructing roughly twenty-six breadboards, close to one per chapter.
claims.quote_verbatim: I have roughly about 20, roughly about 26 breadboards
claims.speaker: Ron Quan
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ron Quan - Tenacious Transistor Teacher

claims.claim_text: Comparative evaluation is done by building rather than reading: an assessment of ten embedded Linux platforms was carried out by physically constructing about thirty-five prototypes.
claims.quote_verbatim: he built like 35 prototypes
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The number of iterations completed is a defensible measure of engineering progress, to the point that one course graded student projects directly on prototype count, provided each revision represented real change rather than a component substitution.
claims.quote_verbatim: you do one prototype, you get a D. You do two prototypes, you get a C. You do three prototypes, you get a B.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Clint Cole of Digilent

claims.claim_text: A toy invention house built roughly two hundred prototypes a year, of which about ten sold and two to four made money, and treated the ability to build almost anything in house — machinists, model makers and sculptors alongside the electronics staff — as the core of the business.
claims.quote_verbatim: that place probably made, I want to say like 200 toy prototypes a year
claims.speaker: Todd Bailey
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Todd Bailey - Embedded Embrasure Engineering

claims.claim_text: The standard held in that shop was that a prototype had to be better than the production article, and a prototype that could not be built as a product was generally not worth making at all.
claims.quote_verbatim: you really don't prototype very much if you know that it's unbuildable
claims.speaker: Todd Bailey
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Todd Bailey - Embedded Embrasure Engineering

claims.claim_text: High prototype throughput is itself the learning mechanism: the value comes from touching many kinds of problem and being able to discard a failed circuit and move on with the lesson rather than defending it.
claims.quote_verbatim: I threw away that turd and moved on to the next circuit with a lesson learned
claims.speaker: Todd Bailey
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Todd Bailey - Embedded Embrasure Engineering

claims.claim_text: Showing the physical object is what closes a sale in a pitch-driven business, because a buyer responds to the thing rather than to a drawing.
claims.quote_verbatim: your sales go up a whole lot when you show someone the thing that they're buying
claims.speaker: Todd Bailey
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Todd Bailey - Embedded Embrasure Engineering

claims.claim_text: Keeping prototype construction in house preserves a hands-on connection that measurably improves design work, and is a deliberate reason to structure a consulting business that way.
claims.quote_verbatim: any prototypes that I need, um, we build them here
claims.speaker: Bob Davidson
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching" with Davidson and Vandenbout - Presbytes Pushing Portfolios

claims.claim_text: A consultant unsure whether a job is achievable prototypes the doubtful part before accepting it, because taking on work and then discovering an insurmountable element is the worst outcome available.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think I can do this, but I'm going to go away, like prototype some little bit of it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mike Harrison - X-ray Examining Xenogogue

claims.claim_text: The rule behind that practice is never to accept work without knowing it can be delivered, which makes a small speculative prototype an instrument of risk management rather than of design.
claims.quote_verbatim: I will never take on something unless I know for sure I can do it.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mike Harrison - X-ray Examining Xenogogue

claims.claim_text: The prototype-to-production handoff is what makes production work unattractive to some consultants: the customer returns months later, by which time everything has to be recalled and the documentation produced.
claims.quote_verbatim: you do the prototype, you give it to the customer, they go away, you go and do something else. Then three months later, they want to put it in production.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Live from Serbia with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: A consultant handling a prototype programme has to state the full sequence to the client in advance — design, prototype build, qualification, and the real possibility that something will need adjustment — rather than quoting the design alone.
claims.quote_verbatim: we're going to have to have the prototypes built and then I'm gonna have to qualify them
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: For a build of about three units, assembling the product from off-the-shelf components is cheaper and faster than a custom design, and the custom product is only worth discussing once volume can amortise the engineering.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you want to just do three, we can buy off the shelf and we can make a prototype for you
claims.speaker: Andrea Longobardi
claims.episode_title: Low Power Connected Devices with Andrea Longobardi

claims.claim_text: Modular sub-assemblies with castellated edges work well in a prototyping context because functions can be swapped in and out, but the space, cost and complexity they add are usually not justified in the final product.
claims.quote_verbatim: are you willing to, you know, use that space and the cost and the overall complexity to put that into your final, final goods?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: An engineer whose electronics knowledge stops at wiring modules together can legitimately deliver a prototype, provided the boundary is stated and a suitably qualified engineer is engaged before production.
claims.quote_verbatim: I admit that I'm only making a prototype
claims.speaker: Elecia White

claims.claim_text: Adding a function through a separate peripheral module rather than an integrated part may not be the optimal design, but the speed it buys is usually worth it at the prototype stage.
claims.quote_verbatim: if it's going to speed up your, your production, it's probably worth it for your, at least your prototype
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: At least my house isn't haunted

claims.claim_text: Prototypes built from the research-and-development parts drawer or from vendor sample bins produce a bill of materials that does not correspond to parts anyone can actually buy, which becomes a problem the moment the design moves forward.
claims.quote_verbatim: We used all the R&D parts and stuff like that. Or we use the sample parts bin
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Component distribution splits by role: catalogue distributors are where prototype and small-run quantities of ten to a hundred are obtained because they hold single-piece stock, while the volume distributors are approached for reels at production quantities.
claims.quote_verbatim: When you need your prototype, you're making 10 or 50 or 100, you don't go to them.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Distribution, Wozniak & Robots - Early Eight-bit Endgame

claims.claim_text: An individual without a registered company can find that suppliers will not sell them parts at all, which is a practical barrier to building a first prototype independently.
claims.quote_verbatim: some people, you know, wouldn't even send me the parts unless I was a company
claims.speaker: Christina Cyr

claims.claim_text: Buying a stock of a scarce connector ahead of need was calculated in prototypes rather than products: two hundred parts covers roughly five to ten prototypes per project across ten or twenty projects, and rework with hot air consumes them faster than that.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's enough for, that's, that's right. That's enough for five to 10 prototypes.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Moving Down The Stack with Scott Williams

claims.claim_text: Twenty-week component lead times can dominate a prototype programme to the point where waiting is the correct decision rather than redesigning around the shortage.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're talking about having more parts in 20 weeks. Maybe you just wait it out.
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: A part that performed correctly in the prototype can still be the wrong part if the qualification work was not done, and at volume the error is only discovered after hundreds of thousands of the part have been committed.
claims.quote_verbatim: It worked great on the prototype, but we didn't do the thorough, you know, thermal testing or whatever
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Prototype debugging can uncover errors in the component vendor's own documentation: repeated destruction of a regulator traced to undocumented back-to-back diodes between the set and output pins, with the vendor's own application circuit exceeding the device's limits.
claims.quote_verbatim: My latest prototype, I've been blowing up LT3080s.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Project Management, Lasers & Robots - Staunch Specialty Sanctanimity

claims.claim_text: In that case the later variants of the same architecture carried a series resistor with the diodes that the original part lacked, implying an undisclosed fix that was never applied to the original device.
claims.quote_verbatim: they've fixed it by putting in a series resistor
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Project Management, Lasers & Robots - Staunch Specialty Sanctanimity

claims.claim_text: A returned prototype has to be verified against the design before it is trusted, because the designer is the one who confirms that the parts fitted are the parts specified.
claims.quote_verbatim: you get it back, you need to verify that that resistor is
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Project Management, Lasers & Robots - Staunch Specialty Sanctanimity

claims.claim_text: Prototype revisions need unique identifiers meaningful enough to name in conversation with a contract manufacturer, because a description in terms of a revision plus whatever firmware happened to be loaded conveys nothing.
claims.quote_verbatim: having like something where it's an actual unique identifier that says something useful
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The rapid-iteration ethos of prototyping — discarding last week's state and moving forward — stops working at the point a contract manufacturer is engaged, where identifiers and records become load-bearing.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you start interacting with a contract manufacturer, that's when it's like, no, no, no, this is real
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Automated design-rule and electrical-rule checks on commit could catch much of what prototypes catch, but hardware still requires the physical build before production; there is no equivalent of pushing a validated change straight through.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've got to physically build the prototype. You can't just push it to production.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Photographing every prototype builds a dated record that makes the year's engineering progress legible after the fact.
claims.quote_verbatim: I always take photos of my prototypes
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The gap between a working prototype and a manufacturable product is where hardware programmes fail: at one consultancy the recurring situation was a client arriving with a development-board prototype that then had to be turned into a real thing, and by the time it reached manufacturing what was built differed from that prototype by nearly every measure.
claims.quote_verbatim: by the time you're in manufacturing, what you build is very different from that original Arduino prototype by almost every measure
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Consulting value at that stage lies in taking someone to a manufacturable product quickly, which is only possible once it is settled what that manufacturable product is.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you don't know what that manufacturable product is yet
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A prototype optimised for hand assembly, printing and locally available parts is effectively a different design from the version a factory will build, so the transition has to be planned as a deliberate design freeze followed by a manufacturable version two.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's almost like you have to, it's almost like a totally different design by the time that you go to a factory.
claims.speaker: Chrissy Meyer

claims.claim_text: Where a design should sit on the spectrum between quick-and-dirty and fully protected against future manufacturing problems has no general answer, and is among the most contested judgements on a startup engineering team.
claims.quote_verbatim: So it's, it's a balancing act.
claims.speaker: Chrissy Meyer

claims.claim_text: There is a real step change between a first prototype and a run of even a hundred units, distinct again from the step to volume manufacturing.
claims.quote_verbatim: There are significant differences from, like, a first prototype to even just a run of a hundred, right?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: One consultancy characterises client readiness as the eighty percent point: a prototype exists and demonstrates the concept, though it might run only two or three minutes before breaking, and the remaining work is taking that into tens or hundreds of thousands of units lasting one or two thousand hours.
claims.quote_verbatim: It might not work more than two or three minutes before it breaks.
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Miller - Sudden SinoAmerican Synthesis

claims.claim_text: Making prototypes and mass manufacturing are different problems of different magnitudes; a vehicle programme that could build prototypes without difficulty was nearly destroyed by manufacturing them.
claims.quote_verbatim: They could make their prototypes, no problems, but mass manufacturing almost killed them.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: A mechanical prototype is not evidence that a mechanical design is close to done: a printed prototype is achievable in a month, whereas the manufacturable design plus its several spins is a different order of work.
claims.quote_verbatim: maybe a prototype, like 3D printed, like prototype, maybe
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeri Ellsworth - Intense Illusion Introduction

claims.claim_text: A well-finished prototype creates a false sense of completion in people who do not build hardware: a solid block of machined ABS matching the industrial design drawings prompted an executive to order twenty-five thousand units of what was still six months from being manufacturable.
claims.quote_verbatim: it looks so real that it like the, that, you know, to, to untrained eye, they think it's done
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The same false sense of completion afflicts the designer: a printed prototype that works can mask defects such as delaminated layers, which get deferred as things to be tweaked later.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can build your prototype and you can get a false sense of completion
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Fake it till you make it

claims.claim_text: The mechanical route from prototype to product introduces problems that the prototype never showed: an enclosure acceptable as a prototype fails once tens of thousands of injection-moulded parts are contemplated, because the mould wears, the plastic sags and the appearance shifts, and the finished product then has to be certified.
claims.quote_verbatim: It looked good as a prototype, but this isn't good when you're going to be shooting 50,000, you know, injection molded plastic pieces.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Regulatory certification is a stage most first-time hardware developers underestimate, and going through it once tends to discourage choosing a custom part over a pre-certified finished module the next time.
claims.quote_verbatim: it just puts you off from going straight to custom the next time
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Handing a prototype to an engineer for productionisation means the engineer produces the engineering drawings and the design-for-manufacture model from a collaborative CAD model rather than from the prototype itself.
claims.quote_verbatim: he'll make engineering drawings based off of that and whatever, like the DFM model will be
claims.speaker: Simone Giertz

claims.claim_text: White-label development inverts the usual order: the starting point is an existing manufacturer's prototype seen in a showroom, which is then modified against the manufacturer's stated capabilities.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's where you start with a prototype
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Hiring a second engineer was what allowed one company to spend the effort on design detail needed to have a product rather than a prototype.
claims.quote_verbatim: make sure we actually have a product and not a prototype
claims.speaker: Jason Cerundolo

claims.claim_text: That programme built on the order of hundreds of prototypes and concentrated its limited engineering resource on the hardest subsystem while pushing the simpler assemblies onto a manufacturing partner.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think we've built somewhere on the order of hundreds of prototypes so far
claims.speaker: Jason Cerundolo

claims.claim_text: Prototypes coming off the contract manufacturer's actual pick-and-place machine, rather than from hand assembly, are the signal that a design has reached manufacturing readiness; a pilot run of tens of units follows.
claims.quote_verbatim: the last couple of prototypes they sent me have been from the actual pick and place machine
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Iterating through ten prototype units with a supplier is how a buyer verifies what hardware that supplier is actually capable of producing before committing to a purchase.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've got 10 different prototypes, you know?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A prototype should never be a single unit: an engineering prototype is built in tens so that the assumptions made during development can be tested against feedback from real users.
claims.quote_verbatim: You're not making one. You're making at least 10.
claims.speaker: Ben Einstein

claims.claim_text: One consumer product failure is characterised as an engineering prototype that was sold at scale: a unit at that maturity should have gone to ten or twenty people known to be testing a beta, to check whether the pricing and the product made sense, not to thousands of paying customers.
claims.quote_verbatim: which should not have been sold by the hundreds or thousands, uh, to end users
claims.speaker: Ben Einstein

claims.claim_text: A single prototype that both functions and looks good produces a step change in a company's valuation, because an investor can interact with the product; reaching that point before tooling, hiring a large factory and spending millions is the objective of early funding.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's this step function value change in the company because people can kind of interact with that product
claims.speaker: Ben Einstein

claims.claim_text: What counts as that prototype is more than the physical part: the website, data path or consumable through which a user interacts with it is part of what has to exist.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's not just a prototype. That's not just a physical part.
claims.speaker: Ben Einstein

claims.claim_text: Early-stage investment is made against a proof of concept that barely works — described as bubble gum, rubber bands and a development board — with the ability to communicate the vision wrapped around it carrying as much weight as the hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's the, it's the bubble gum and rubber bands and a, you know, a dev board.

claims.claim_text: Having working prototypes to show distinguishes a hardware startup from the substantial proportion that are presenting an idea alone, and bootstrapping the early units is treated as evidence of seriousness.
claims.quote_verbatim: having the prototypes to show is, I mean, that's ahead of a lot of startups
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An interview with Jeri Ellsworth - Absorptive Augmented Actuality

claims.claim_text: The counter to scepticism about a hardware claim is physical inspection rather than more video material: inviting doubtful parties to handle the prototype in person was the successful approach where supplying videos and materials was not.
claims.quote_verbatim: stop by the Maker Faire booth and like kick the tires
claims.speaker: Jeri Ellsworth
claims.episode_title: An interview with Jeri Ellsworth - Absorptive Augmented Actuality

claims.claim_text: A prototype in hand is what secures the meeting: having something to show is the difference between competing on a proposal and competing on a demonstration.
claims.quote_verbatim: So was it advantageous to have that prototype to take the meetings
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A pattern in startups is to build a rough prototype, secure press coverage of it, and use that coverage as a springboard to further meetings.
claims.quote_verbatim: you make some janky prototype and then you go like get Engadget and a bunch of companies to talk about it
claims.speaker: Jeri Ellsworth
claims.episode_title: Jeri Ellsworth and the demise of CastAR

claims.claim_text: Investor meetings are a non-renewable resource: going out to raise without working prototypes and showing hardware the same investors had already seen consumed the whole pool of available investors for that company.
claims.quote_verbatim: we had no prototypes that worked at the time
claims.speaker: Jeri Ellsworth
claims.episode_title: Jeri Ellsworth and the demise of CastAR

claims.claim_text: Time spent on activities such as repeated rebranding is time not spent on prototypes, and that displacement is a direct engineering cost in a startup.
claims.quote_verbatim: that means you're also not working on prototypes
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Jeri Ellsworth and the demise of CastAR

claims.claim_text: An applicant to an accelerator without a working prototype is advised to assemble a half-working one and show it to people directly before interviews, or failing that to bring other hardware as evidence of capability.
claims.quote_verbatim: I would have together a half working prototype and start showing it to people personally
claims.speaker: Luke Iseman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Iseman of yCombinator

claims.claim_text: Customers repeatedly failed to engage with paper, cardboard and metal models of a device, and only began treating the project seriously once a prototype existed that could make a call and receive a text — even though the internals were not the intended design.
claims.quote_verbatim: people wouldn't take me seriously
claims.speaker: Christina Cyr

claims.claim_text: That outcome runs against the taught sequence of validating with a drawing, then a cardboard prototype, then progressively more resilient models before building anything complete.
claims.quote_verbatim: you shouldn't build a single thing until you show them a piece of paper and a drawing
claims.speaker: Christina Cyr

claims.claim_text: Smaller and less established customers are the ones willing to trial an unproven prototype in their operations; larger and better-resourced ones require substantially more assurance before allowing it near their equipment.
claims.quote_verbatim: And they're the ones who are willing to try out the prototypes.
claims.speaker: Ronald Sousa
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ronald Sousa of Hash Define Electronics

claims.claim_text: Crowdfunding platforms came to require that campaigns show real hardware rather than renderings or simulations, forcing applicants to do the up-front work and spend their own money on a prototype before raising.
claims.quote_verbatim: They now no longer allow simulations or 3D, you know, those fancy 3D rendered models.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, Manufacturing, Open Hardware - Judging Jurisdictional Junctures

claims.claim_text: The rationale is that an appealing product concept costs nothing to render, so requiring photographs of real hardware is what separates projects with engineering behind them from those without.
claims.quote_verbatim: You're only allowed to show real photos of real hardware.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, Manufacturing, Open Hardware - Judging Jurisdictional Junctures

claims.claim_text: The recognisable failure signature before that rule was a campaign with an aggressive delivery date, a rendered video and no hardware; requests to see any earlier prototype went unanswered.
claims.quote_verbatim: They had no real product, no real prototype.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, IndieGoGo & Ignite - Jasperated Jimswinger Jobbery

claims.claim_text: Campaigns that repeatedly describe spinning more boards while never showing an earlier one are describing work that does not exist.
claims.quote_verbatim: People keep asking them, show us an old prototype.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, IndieGoGo & Ignite - Jasperated Jimswinger Jobbery

claims.claim_text: Choice of crowdfunding platform can itself signal prototype maturity, since a campaign lacking hardware may run on a platform that does not require it.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's a reason why it's on Indiegogo and not on Kickstarter because they don't have a prototype
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Tesla, FPGAs and DigiKey - Zesty Zippy Zynq

claims.claim_text: The obligation defended is that the developer funds the prototype themselves rather than raising money to build the first one, however crude the result.
claims.quote_verbatim: Go and spend your own money and produce the prototype. Make it out of cardboard.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The Art Of Staying Interested In Electronics - Exponible Electronics Ennui

claims.claim_text: A prototype requirement is only as strong as the standard applied to it: a demonstration whose performance falls far short of the campaign's claims, on the argument that funding will close the gap, satisfies the letter of the rule and not its purpose.
claims.quote_verbatim: your prototype does not match your claims
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Amazon Moves In, Dave Says Run

claims.claim_text: Having produced a prototype is not evidence of the ability to manufacture: an applicant may arrive with a working unit and still lack the experience, or carry the feature-creep tendency that sinks funded projects once money arrives.
claims.quote_verbatim: They may walk in with their prototype, which they've produced, but they may be absolutely clueless.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: B Plus Boards and D Minus Cities - Uneath Urban Ubication

claims.claim_text: A stronger requirement than a prototype is a completed pilot run and a bill of materials, since only a build produces realistic costs.
claims.quote_verbatim: You have to have done a proto run.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Documentation Is A Waste Of Time

claims.claim_text: Large companies build prototypes at a steady institutional rate — twenty or thirty a year within a single design group — which is what makes a prototyping service a repeatable business rather than a one-off one.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you're, if you're making 20, 30 prototypes a year at one of these larger companies
claims.episode_title: CircuitHub, 12 Years Later with Andrew Seddon

claims.claim_text: The first version of a custom chip was built deliberately as a prototype rather than a product, with the explicit purpose of raising enough money to assemble a team.
claims.quote_verbatim: The first one was really just to get enough money so I can get a team together.
claims.speaker: Andreas Olofsson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Andreas Olofsson - Adapteva's Ampliative Abacus

claims.claim_text: Treating an early silicon spin as an intentional throwaway is a recognised strategy, described as version zero and an intentional punt.
claims.quote_verbatim: So I would call that an intentional punt, right? Prototype. That was version zero.
claims.speaker: Andreas Olofsson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Andreas Olofsson - Adapteva's Ampliative Abacus

claims.claim_text: A respin can be caused by a vendor's error rather than the designer's, in which case the vendor may bear the cost.
claims.quote_verbatim: one of our vendors made a mistake, and so we had to spin it
claims.speaker: Andreas Olofsson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Andreas Olofsson - Adapteva's Ampliative Abacus

claims.claim_text: Cheap access to fabrication moves the money spent from an idea to a prototype, so a customer or investor can evaluate a real design rather than a theoretical one without funding a toolchain first.
claims.quote_verbatim: to move the money from the idea to the prototype
claims.speaker: Mohamed Kassem
claims.episode_title: Fabless Chip Design with Mohamed Kassem

claims.claim_text: Historically some advertised products existed only as prototypes or proof-of-concept models, placed in the market to test for interest on the assumption that a buyer would justify making them work.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think did not exist outside of prototypes or proof of concept models
claims.episode_title: The Space Time Continuum with Fran Blanche

claims.claim_text: Early prototypes of foundational technologies were notably crude, which is characteristic of genuinely new work rather than a mark against it.
claims.quote_verbatim: the relative crudeness of a lot of prototypes
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: A complete prototype comprising a fabricated board, printed mechanical parts and assembly can be produced for on the order of a hundred dollars, a benchmark stable enough to be tracked over time like a basket of goods.
claims.quote_verbatim: what is the type of prototype you could build for a hundred dollars?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Reaching that hundred-dollar figure requires everything delivered — the one-off board, the laser-cut case, the printed parts and the components — not just the board.
claims.quote_verbatim: You've got to get the PCB one off. You've got to get it delivered.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A convincingly fit-and-finished prototype adequate for a promotional video can be produced for well under ten thousand dollars using laser cutting and printing, unless the object is large or made from formed metal.
claims.quote_verbatim: you could totally do that for like less than 10 grand
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: First prototypes do not require large capital: a handful of first articles can be built for around a thousand dollars, and a dozen units were built entirely by hand.
claims.quote_verbatim: Everyone thinks that they have to spend a shitload of money to get initial prototypes done. You don't.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ian Daniher - Nascent Nonolith Numquid

claims.claim_text: Thinking about prototype spend in unit prices conceals the cash requirement: a hundred-dollar unit cost becomes twenty thousand dollars at a two hundred unit pilot, and running out of cash at that transition is a common cause of failure.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you have a hundred dollar prototype or a hundred dollar cost to
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: In-house board milling suits quick rough prototypes only, since it produces neither solder mask nor plated-through holes; for simple analogue work a board can be cut in about two hours.
claims.quote_verbatim: They're okay for really quick in-house, you know, rough prototypes.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Funding New/Manufacturing Old Projects - Radical Robotic Requisition

claims.claim_text: A solder paste dispensing machine at around ten thousand dollars is flexible enough to paste a board from its Gerber data without a stencil, but is slow enough to suit one-off prototypes and rework rather than production.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's good for like one-off prototypes and things
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: In-house reflow equipment is justified against the prototypes it saves rather than its price alone, and increasingly complex boards including ball-grid-array assemblies are being built locally that would previously have been sent to an assembly house.
claims.quote_verbatim: you think about how many prototypes i potentially destroyed
claims.speaker: Saber Kaygusuz

claims.claim_text: Flexible circuits earn their place in prototypes that must fit a small awkward volume, and are worth fabricating in house only if the turnaround is on the order of an hour; otherwise ordering a flex board is the better route.
claims.quote_verbatim: little complex prototypes that have to, you know, form fit in some sort of, you know, little tiny volume
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Building a prototype oneself before engaging a specialist firm is a way of formulating and communicating the requirement, with the professional engaged afterwards to make the result robust.
claims.quote_verbatim: If I can like prototype something before I go talk to a professional firm or engineer
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The proof-of-concept stage can be skipped entirely in some workflows: once the circuit exists on breadboard or veroboard, going straight to the production board avoids an intermediate one-off build that teaches little.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'd jump from that straight to the production PCB
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A complete prototype comprising a cheaply fabricated board with inexpensive parts and a printed mechanical section was estimated at under a hundred dollars once free schematic and modelling tools were available, at the cost of considerable effort and an unpolished result.
claims.quote_verbatim: you could probably make an entire prototype for less than $100
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Analog Devices, Design Spark - Unusual Usenet Usurpation

claims.claim_text: Custom enclosures are the expensive element of a prototype: where one is genuinely required, it costs both money and time to produce.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a pain in the ass to prototype. It costs you money to prototype and time.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Sourcing components — finding parts, buying them, opening packaging and organising them — is a substantial and usually unaccounted share of the effort in prototype work.
claims.quote_verbatim: especially for prototype type stuff, that's a huge part of it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Get Smart About Automation - Caducous Cyborg Concerns

claims.claim_text: Development boards and finished products are different engineering problems, the former being less complex and more narrowly specified than a general product.
claims.quote_verbatim: They do more development boards and stuff, which are easier than
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Get Smart About Automation - Caducous Cyborg Concerns

claims.claim_text: A personal project built to prototype standard functions as evidence of capability when approaching an employer or client, even without commercial work behind it.
claims.quote_verbatim: here's this thing I did. Here's a prototype I worked on.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: PCBs, Tektronix & Ham Radio - Habitual Handicraft Hangups

claims.claim_text: It is now feasible for a single person to take a design as far as a working prototype or proof of concept without a multi-person company behind them.
claims.quote_verbatim: how much of a prototype or proof of concept you can get out the door as a one-person dev shop
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
